text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryThe Mysterious Migrant Potters of Ancient Tampa BayAnother archaeological cold case solvedJCBy Jake Currie3:00 PM CDT on September 22, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBefore European explorers arrived in the United States, the native Mississippian culture thrived across the midwestern and southeastern parts of the country. Known for the mounds they built and their intricate pottery designs, several of these cultural variants flourished for centuries, from 1,000 to around 1,600 CE. How far south they ranged has been the subject of some debate, but a new study published in American Antiquity finds compelling evidence of Mississippian migrants ranging as far south as Tampa Bay for the first time. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 1057.5K 20Could This Be The End of Hangovers? Science Thinks SoShareNextStayAnthropologists from the University of Florida and the Florida Museum of Natural History came to that conclusion after meticulously studying pottery shards recovered from the area nearly a century ago.
